questions.question: A unit whole-life death benefit is deferred $u>0$ years: it pays only if future lifetime $T>u$. What happens if the life dies before time u?
options: The benefit is paid at time u after the waiting period ends.
The benefit is paid immediately because death triggers every whole-life contract.
No benefit is due for that death.
The benefit is carried forward until a later annual settlement boundary.

questions.question: A unit whole-life death benefit begins coverage only after deferment $u>0$ years. The insured is alive at time u. Does survival to that date itself trigger the benefit?
options: Yes; one unit is paid immediately upon reaching u.
Yes; reaching u triggers all future annual instalments.
No; surviving to u ends the coverage instead.
No; it activates cover for a later death.

questions.question: A life currently alive has continuous future lifetime $T>0$ almost surely. A unit death benefit pays at T only when $T>u$. What contract is obtained at deferment $u=0$?
options: An annual-settlement whole-life benefit, regardless of its stated death-time payment.
Ordinary whole-life insurance with immediate payment at death.
A survival benefit paid immediately at issue.
A contract with no covered deaths because the waiting period has zero length.

questions.question: A unit death benefit is paid immediately at a qualifying death time $0<u<T<\infty$ after deferment u. With annual discount factor $v>0$, $v\ne1$, which factor values that payment at the original issue date?

A continuous lifetime $T$ is used to price a deferred benefit at death with waiting time $u\ge0$ and positive discount factor $v$. Would replacing the coverage condition $T>u$ by $T\ge u$ change its APV?
options: Yes; the weak condition adds every death before u.
Yes; the weak condition makes the benefit a payment at time u.
No; the two conditions differ only on a zero-probability death time.
No; the two coverage events are identical as sets.

questions.question: A unit death benefit pays at the death time only if $T>u$, where the unknown deferment is $u\ge0$. A realised benefit was paid at death time $T=3$ years. Which range of deferments is compatible with this observed payment?
options: $0\le u\le3$.

questions.question: A deferred unit death benefit has issue-to-coverage-start pure-endowment factor $E=0.7$. Conditional on reaching that date, the older-age whole-life APV is $b=0.4$ at the same settlement convention. What is its issue APV?
options: $0.571429$ approximately.

questions.question: A unit whole-life death benefit paid at death has APV $0.5$. Its initial coverage for deaths at or before time u has APV $0.2$ on the same mortality and interest basis. What is APV of the complementary benefit for deaths after u?

A unit death benefit covers only deaths after time $u=2$. It uses annual settlement at the end of the year of death. The realised death time is $T=1.8$, so its annual boundary is time two. Is a benefit paid?
options: Yes; settlement occurs at the deferment endpoint.
No; the death occurred before coverage began.
Yes; any death in the second year is included after two-year deferment.
No; annual settlement would instead wait until time three.

questions.question: Death occurs at a finite time almost surely. At zero interest, a unit death benefit pays only when $T>u$, and $\mathbb{P}(T>u)=0.6$. What is its APV?

For deferment $u\ge0$ and annual discount $v>0$, with $s=\mathbb{P}(T>u)>0$, let $b$ be the unit whole-life APV among survivors at u, using their conditional remaining-lifetime law. Does the identity $D=v^usb$ for issue deferred APV D require survival and later lifetime to be independent?
options: Yes; every product of actuarial factors requires independent events.
Yes; later survival must always equal original-age survival.
No; b can instead use any unrelated mortality law.
No; b already uses the law conditional on surviving to u.

questions.question: Use the same lifetime random variable T and positive annual discount factor v. A unit benefit pays at T only if T exceeds deferment u. Assume both compared APVs are finite. Which statement about increasing u holds for every such lifetime model?
options: It cannot increase, regardless of whether v is above or below one.
It increases whenever v is greater than one.
It is unchanged because every remaining payment still has size one.
It can be compared only if the later conditional whole-life price decreases with age.

questions.question: A deferred unit death benefit pays at finite death time T only if $T>u$, with $u>0$, annual discount $0<v<1$ and survival probability $s=\mathbb{P}(T>u)>0$. What bound must its issue APV D satisfy?
options: $D=v^u s$ in every such mortality model.
$D>v^u s$.
$D\ge s$.

questions.question: A life has constant mortality force $\lambda=0.1$ per year and interest force $\delta=0.2$ per year. A unit benefit pays at death only after two-year deferment. What is its APV?
A lifetime T is uniform on $(0,4)$ years. At zero interest, a unit deferred death benefit covers only deaths with $1<T<3$ and pays at death. What is its APV?

A continuous lifetime T has curtate death-year count $K=\lfloor T\rfloor$ with masses $0.2,0.3,0.5$ at $0,1,2$. A unit death benefit is deferred two years and uses annual settlement with discount factor $v=0.5$. What is its APV?

A lifetime T is uniform on $(0.5,1)$ years, and original annual death settlement is at $\lceil T\rceil$. Cover is deferred to $u=0.5$, with discount $v=0.81$. Does multiplying the time-u annual whole-life price by $v^u\mathbb{P}(T>u)$ preserve the original payment grid?
options: Yes; discount multiplication works for every real-valued deferment.
No; the shifted annual contract settles at time 1.5 instead of time one.
No; financial discount factors are defined only at integer times.
No; a continuous death model cannot use annual settlement.

questions.question: Let finite deferred APVs be $D(u)=\mathbb{E}[v^T\mathbf1_{\{T>u\}}]$ and $D(w)=\mathbb{E}[v^T\mathbf1_{\{T>w\}}]$, where $0\le u<w$ are finite and $v>0$. If the two prices are equal, what must follow?
options: The conclusion requires v to be at most one.
$\mathbb{P}(T>u)=0$.
$\mathbb{P}(u<T\le w)=0$.
The two conditional older-age whole-life APVs must be equal.

questions.question: A continuous lifetime has $S(1)=0.8,S(2)=0.6$ and discount $v=0.5$. Deferred death benefits pay at death, with quoted APVs $D(1)=0.15,D(2)=0.10$. Can both quotes fit the model?
options: No; their difference requires all intervening deaths exactly at time two.
Yes; their difference equals a permitted weak discount bound for that window.
No; their difference must equal the unweighted death probability 0.2.
Yes; every supplied probability and price is between zero and one.

questions.question: A lifetime T is uniform on $(0,4)$ years, and discount force is $\delta=\log2$, so $v=1/2$. A unit benefit is paid at death only after two-year deferment. Which approximate issue-date APV uses the actual conditional older-age mortality basis?
